Date: Friday, June 12, 2026

Execution order (follow this exactly):
1. Lock the direction — You pick one of the three mockups above (plus any per-option notes). I am choosing option B and everything that comes with it along with the decisions I gave you in the questions you asked me. That selection becomes a new, separate implementation story; the steps below are the build plan for whichever direction wins.
2. Study the reference pages first — Read my-profile so the redesign reuses the established card / row / icon patterns. Read, especially, the current tab3 implementation covering the "FRED" logo display. Copy all the SCSS/styling associated with that for both the clickable white shadowy version and the non white shadowy un-clickable version to the new layout.
3. Preserve the data + behavior — Keep the settingSections array, the *ngFor rows, onSettingClick(action), goToMyProfile(), onFredLogoClick() MFU interaction, and the profileActionRequired$ badge wired exactly as-is — this is HTML + SCSS only, no .ts logic rewrite.
4. Rebuild tab3.page.html + .scss — Implement the chosen direction: restyle the blue header (carrying safe-area-top), the three grouped sections, and the footer. FRED palette + Manrope + Material Symbols only.
5. Verify & check for regressions — Run npx tsc --noEmit (exits 0), confirm the header clears the notch and the full list fits at 390×844 and 430×932, re-test every settings row still routes correctly and the FRED-logo MFU tap still fires, then run the verifier agent.

Andrew's Answers:
FRED-192: Which direction do you want built? Pick one of the three mockups above (tap to select). My recommendation is Option A — Elevated Grouped Cards because it's the most consistent with the white-section-card pattern your other migrated pages just standardized on, and it's the lowest-risk "cleaner" win. Use the per-option note boxes if you want to mix elements (e.g. "A's cards but B's hero stat strip").
            Required: i think option B and everything that comes with option B

Design feedback per option:
Design feedback — Option B — Hero Stat Header: i like this design a lot. the only thing i want you to do before implementing this is to look at the current tab3 implementation covering the "FRED" display. copy all the scss associated with that for both the clickable white shadowy version and the non white shadowy unclickable version

Proceed with implementation.
